compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Discovered while confirming the root cause of `enchanting-phantastic-weevil`
(a61d-adf9-3725-4847). Independent of that ticket's scheme-downgrade concern, and deliberately
left out of its scope.

`location /review/` proxies with a prefix-STRIPPING form
(`proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/;`, `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:104`), so the
review-bot app never sees the `/review/` prefix. When the app emits an ABSOLUTE redirect it builds
it from the public `Host` header, so the emitted path has no `/review/` prefix to strip — and the
prefix is simply lost.

## Observed (deployed edge, unauthenticated)

    GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/health/
      -> HTTP/2 307, location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health

The correct target is `…/review/health`. `…/health` matches no review-bot location, falls through
to `location /` -> Gerrit, and 404s. So a client that follows the redirect lands on a 404 instead
of the health endpoint. Same for `/review/webhook/` -> `…/webhook` and `/review/rerun/` ->
`…/rerun`.

## Why this is separate from a61d

a61d owns one invariant: an https request must never receive a `Location` that downgrades the
scheme to `http`. Fixing that (trusting the forwarded proto + a `proxy_redirect` http->https
backstop) makes the header `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health` — correct scheme, still
the wrong path. The residual is path correctness, not a security downgrade, and folding it into
a61d would widen that ticket's blast radius past what its plan covers.

## Candidate approach (NOT yet verified)

A per-location `proxy_redirect` that restores the prefix, e.g.
`proxy_redirect https://$host/ https://$host/review/;` alongside a61d's rules — but this must be
checked against every absolute URL the app can emit, because it would also rewrite a deliberate
redirect to a non-`/review/` target. The alternative is to stop stripping the prefix and mount the
app under `/review` (a root_path / APIRouter prefix change), which is a larger, app-side change.
Establish which before implementing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] It is established which absolute URLs the review-bot app can emit, so a prefix-restoring
      rewrite is known not to corrupt a legitimate non-`/review/` redirect.
- [ ] A request to `https://<host>/review/<route>/` receives a `Location` whose path retains the
      `/review/` prefix, verified by a structural test over the rendered nginx config (or by the
      app-side mount, whichever approach is chosen).
- [ ] The existing prefix-stripping request behaviour is unchanged: `GET /review/health` still
      reaches the app as `GET /health` and returns 200.
- [ ] LIVE VALIDATION: an unauthenticated probe of `/review/health/` on the deployed edge shows a
      `Location` that resolves to the health endpoint rather than a Gerrit 404, recorded in a
      comment with the actual response headers.

## Notes

Reported from unauthenticated probes and repo inspection only. No credential was transmitted.
compiled_state.title: /review/ redirects lose the /review/ prefix, so the Location 404s on Gerrit
